messages:
sam: Heads-up — after the kernel swap to rotary/kernels v2 we started hitting NaNs in the ROPE/ALiBi stability suite for long sequences (>=8192). Failing test: attn_rope_longseq_fp16.test. Minimal repro in a comment below.

ci-bot: CI failed: attn_rope_longseq_fp16 on ubuntu-gpu-1 (a100). Logs: stack trace shows NaN in attention weights, test marked flaky -> red. Issue created: #5231. :warning:

chris: I reproduced locally on my devbox (fp16 build). Narrowed it down to the angle computation inside the fused rotary kernel — we do inv_freq * pos in fp16 and then call sin/cos. For large pos values the argument explodes and sin/cos returns NaN/inf in some hardware kernels.

maya: Ugh. That matches what I saw a while back. Two quick ideas: 1) compute the angles in fp32 (either precompute table or cast inside kernel) and then downcast; 2) remap angles to [-pi, pi] before sin/cos (mod reduction). Both avoid catastrophic fp16 precision loss.

ana: For ALiBi: the bias is computed as pos * slope where slope depends on pow(10000, -2i/d). When quantized and multiplied in fp16 we can hit denorms/overflow depending on ordering of ops. Using log-space or fused exp-multiply can be much more stable.

lee: Tradeoff note: precomputing an fp32 table for huge seq lengths increases memory (O(seq_len * dim/2)) and precompute time, but it's cheap compared to paying for NaNs/debug time. If we precompute on CPU we also introduce transfer latency.

sam: Proposal: two-pronged fix — (A) inside the fused kernel, compute angle accumulation in f32 (accumulate pos*inv_freq in f32) then compute sincos in f32 and cast to fp16 for the multiply; (B) add an alternate codepath that precomputes fp32 sin/cos table for seq_len > 4096 and uses fast lookup. Make (B) a fallback to avoid perf regressions in usual cases.

chris: Sounds good. I tossed together a tiny repro showing fp16 path NaN:

```
// repro.cu (very small)
half a = make_half(1.0f);
for (int pos=0; pos<10000; ++pos) {
  half angle = __hmul(a, __float2half(inv_freq*pos)); // fp16 multiplication
  float af = __half2float(angle);
  float s = sinf(af);
  if (!isfinite(s)) { printf("NaN at pos=%d\n", pos); break; }
}
```

maya: Nice repro. Two followups: 1) we should check bfloat16 on TPUs/GPUs that support it — bfloat preserves exponent range and may avoid this entirely; 2) check interaction with quantized models where we scale QKV after or before posenc multiply.

ana: Also should add a numerical stability unit: generate random inv_freq and pos combos (1..16384) and assert finite +/- relative error vs fp32 reference. Make that part of CI (attn_stability_longseq).

lee: On the interface side, where to put this switch? I'd rather not add ad-hoc flags sprinkled in kernels. Suggestion: extend kernel-selector config with posenc.precision: [auto, f16_fast, f32_stable, precompute_fp32]. Default=auto where selector uses (seq_len, dtype, hw) heuristics to pick. Will update selector logic in kernel-selector RFC follow-up.

sam: Good. I'll draft the RFC addendum to kernel selection today — will propose the new posenc.precision knob and heuristics (auto -> precompute_fp32 if seq_len>8192 on fp16, else f32_stable on Ampere when needed).

chris: I'll run perf numbers for 2k/8k seq with both approaches. Quick note: f32 sincos in-kernel is ~1.1x slower than fp16 sincos but avoids NaNs. Precompute fp32 table with texture-like gather is actually faster at inference for large batches because repeated kernel work amortizes.

ci-bot: Created issue #5231 (attn_rope_longseq_fp16) and CI job attn_stability_longseq added to nightly.

lee: I'll open the kernel PR today (branch: fix/rope-alibi-numeric-stability). Plan: add f32-accumulation path + selector flag + unit tests. Will target canary dedicated first, then hosted.

sam: Thanks — plan summary: Lee -> PR for kernel + tests, Sam -> RFC addendum and selector heuristics, Chris -> perf runs, Ana/Maya -> add numeric fuzz tests/quantization checks. Ping @here if regressions crop up. :thumbsup:
